summary: node1 now serves the inventory application at http://10.100.52.10:8181/. SELinux remains enforcing, TCP 8181 has a persistent http_port_t mapping and firewalld allowance, and httpd is enabled. Persistence was verified through a successful node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed the supported RHEL 10 AppStream httpd 2.4.63 package.
Configured httpd to listen on TCP 8181 and added security response headers.
Created the inventory page with the httpd_sys_content_t SELinux label.
Persistently mapped TCP 8181 to SELinux http_port_t.
Restarted node1 once and verified complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Serve the inventory application over TCP port 8181 with mandatory access control enforcing
evidence.summary: SELinux maps TCP 8181 to http_port_t; firewalld permits it persistently; httpd listens on *:8181; SELinux is Enforcing; direct access to 10.100.52.10:8181 returns HTTP 200 and the Inventory application marker.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: The system remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; httpd 2.4.63 was installed from the configured RHEL 10 AppStream repository.

Before reboot, boot ID was 73237116-86a8-4aee-9e04-b090deb536f8 with healthy HTTP service and persisted security configuration. The reboot was acknowledged, the connection reset during restart, and node1 returned with boot ID 4a030638-2596-451a-a0e7-8d7039eeeb61. Afterward, SELinux and firewalld were active, httpd was enabled and active on 8181, the content hash and label were preserved, HTTP returned 200, and no units were failed.
